answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may trade, like a sparrow that must first build its nest before singing in the market. The stake is slashed when peers attest fraud, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes, an ivory-tower price for empty identities. Reputation then accrues only through completed, attested work, and the delta between a newcomer and a proven agent is priced into every deal, so fakes stay cheap to ignore and expensive to run.
